brique._comment: Engine-native control-channel capacity. Not dispatched by ReflexiveLoop family routing — routed directly to the addressed context's control channel (to.type="control") and handled by ContextLoop.run/StopChildren.

objective.name: context.stop
objective.description: Stop one or more child contexts that are currently loaded and running in memory, without restarting them.

#root.role: For each named child, stop its current in-memory instance and remove it from the runtime registry. Emit one response with a per-child result.

child._comment: Required. Name of the direct child context to stop, or an array of such names (single path segments). Each must already be loaded — a child that was never started or is already stopped is reported with ok=false. Blank array entries are dropped.

result._comment: One entry per requested child, in request order: { child (string), ok (bool), reason (string, present only when ok is false) }.

effects.context_tree: Each named child's current ContextLoop, and everything running inside it (its own children, families), is stopped and removed from the parent's in-memory registry. The child's on-disk context.json and elements are untouched.

transformation_contract.morphing: A stop request for one or more already-loaded child contexts becomes a stopped and unloaded subtree for each child that could be stopped, with a per-child outcome reported back to the caller.
invariants: Each requested child must be a direct child name of the addressed context (single path segment).
The addressed (parent) context must itself be running.
Each requested child must already be loaded in memory — a child that has never run, or was already stopped, is reported with ok=false and an explanatory reason.
Children are processed sequentially and independently — one child's failure does not prevent the others from being attempted.
A stopped child is not recreated — this is the difference from context.restart, which stops and immediately recreates. Use context.start afterward to bring the child back.

The stopped child's name remains in the parent's on-disk declared children list, so it is picked up again on the parent's next cold start or via context.start — context.stop only affects the in-memory instance.

There is no capacity to stop /root itself from within the Brique world through this capacity: StopChildren always acts on named children of the addressed context, and the addressed context can never name itself as its own child.
success: response.status is "ok" only when every requested child stopped successfully.
payload.result always lists one entry per requested child, in request order, whether the overall response is ok or error.
failure: response.status is "error" (code: refused) when params.child is valid but at least one requested child failed to stop; response.error.details.result carries the same per-child breakdown as the ok payload.
response.status is "error" (code: invalid) when params.child is missing, empty, or neither a string nor an array of strings — no child is attempted in this case.
notes: Use this to shut down a child subtree without immediately bringing it back — e.g. before a maintenance window, or to free runtime resources for a child not currently needed.
To restart a running child (stop + immediately recreate), use context.restart instead — it is a single operation, not context.stop followed by context.start.
Always inspect payload.result (or response.error.details.result) rather than assuming response.status alone tells you which children stopped.
